sentences.text: Rule twenty-six covers vessels engaged in fishing, and remember from lesson two what that means: gear that restricts her maneuverability.
These lights apply whether she’s underway or at anchor.
A trawler shows two all-round lights: green over white.
She also carries a masthead light behind and above the green one, though a trawler under fifty meters doesn’t have to.
Off this coast, that’s your shrimp boat.
A vessel fishing any other way shows red over white.
And when her gear reaches out more than one hundred fifty meters from her, she adds an all-round white light in the direction of the gear.
So which side do you pass on?
Stay away from that white light.
One more thing for both kinds.
When she’s making way through the water, she adds sidelights and a sternlight.
No sidelights means she’s fishing but not making way.
